profile_md: Northwestern has a distributed set of employer-linked group routes rather than one institution-wide scheme. The widest is Design Thinking and Communication (ENG/DSGN 106-1/-2), a two-quarter course compulsory for first-year McCormick Engineering students and open to any undergraduate (2026-27 listing); student teams tackle design problems submitted by individuals, non-profits, entrepreneurs and industry members, with partners checking in over ten weeks and receiving a proof-of-concept. The partner mix includes individuals, so partner type is Mixed. McCormick programmes add IEMS 394 client projects (named clients such as JetBlue, Lurie Children's Hospital and Coca-Cola Consolidated in 2025-26; team basis not confirmed), the MMM Business Innovation Lab (teams of 4-6 for company problems) and the MLDS industry practicum/capstone (groups of 3-4). Kellogg runs many client-project labs; MKTG 650 Marketing Consulting Lab (teams of 5-6 with a client, 10 weeks) was verified. Medill's Cause Marketing Initiative places IMC teams with nonprofits. Several of these pages are undated, so current delivery is only confirmed for DTC and IEMS 394. Internal Northwestern units appear among some IEMS projects and are not counted. Arts, humanities and social science leads and the science area remain unverified beyond search summaries.
gaps: Reduced-depth review. Not verified: ME 398 and other departmental capstones (PDF unreadable); remaining Kellogg labs; Segal mpd2/MaDE; Civic Engagement Certificate, Crafting Child Policy and Professional Linkage Seminar (search summaries only; class page 404); Medill Immersion Quarter; IEMS 394 team basis and compulsory status; DTC credit and partner mix; participation numbers throughout. Several McCormick/Medill/MMM/MLDS pages are undated (current status unclear). Further departmental instances likely.
